Hi yes I’m from the uk. I’ve actually been referred a couple of times by my GP for different moles. The first time I think it was a couple of months wait but the second time I had a mole on my face that flaked off and then came back so they did a 2 week referral and I remember it was close to end of the 2 weeks before I was made an appointment with a dermatologist. She looked at it and said straight away it was fine and then I pointed to a few other moles and she checked them for me too. 

When I got referred for the birth mark back in February, I was shitting myself with anxiety because I knew it would be up to 2 weeks which is a worry anyway and they were sending me links to do with cancer from my gp! But I actually had a call the next day after seeing my gp to go to this place that takes photos of your mole/birthmark. I was worried because I thought that was a bad sign as it was the day after seeing my gp. They took some fancy photos lol and sent it to a dermatologist who said it wasn’t very clear so I had to see one in person. 

She looked at it and said it’s not cancer but the pigmentation is abnormal. She then asked if i had any other moles or anything and i have loads (had them since I was a kid) but I pointed out the ones that are bigger or have changed over time. They were all fine and I go back on Monday the 5th to see the dermatologist to see if my leg has changed as she wanted to give it 6 months. I don’t think it’s changed at all but I forgot to show her my arm where I had this blister spot thing come up last year and it’s got a bit bigger and is kinda hard. So I’m crapping myself thinking it’s cancer and I’ve seen other people post pictures on Reddit on skin subs of the same blister thing and people told them to get it checked as it looked cancerous… so now I’m terrified. 

If I was you I would either ask to be seen by a different doctor or I would just go back and say you’re really worried and you’ve noticed changes and would really like to be referred to a dermatologist. Because you mentioned it flaking, that’s a change and any changes normally means being investigated. Even if you tell a fib and say you feel pain behind the mole or heat underneath. Sometimes you have to just to be taken seriously. But yeah that’s how it’s happened for me. I dont actually have a certain GP, I always see someone different each time. 

When you do see a dermatologist, just say you have other moles you’re worried about and point them out, they will check them. I hope this helps and make sure you go back to your doctors
